messages:
Mae: heads-up — canary for release/3382 is showing a 2.3x increase in p99 generation latency on the 2nd-stage canary cluster (eu-west). KV cache hit rate dropped from ~82% to ~46%. Not a small blip, rolling back paused.
Rajiv: ugh. Did the canary logs show errors or a spike in cache evictions?
Mae: eviction rate jumped ~4x around the same time. attaching quick flame output below.
Mae: ```
flamegraph: choose_kernel_for_seq -> batch_builder -> kv_cache::lookup_maybe -> remote_fetch
hot path: choose_kernel_for_seq (50%)
seq_len_hist: 2..8 tokens increased in frequency (was 12..64 before)
```
Sam: So the kernel selection heuristic picked a different kernel because seq_len distribution shifted (more short requests), and that kernel has worse interoperability with our KV cache warm path?
Tanya: It looks like the new batching heuristic in 3382 biases to bigger batches when input lengths vary; if it incorrectly groups many short sequences with long ones it can blow through prefix cache locality.
Oliver: Did perf-bot post any CI perf regression alerts for the merge?
perf-bot: Regression detected in CI/perf/perf-latency-mean (job id: 60421) on PR #3382: p99 gen latency +68% (threshold 15%). See: https://ci.internal/reports/60421
Rajiv: I ran a local repro on a smaller dogfood cluster: toggling the heuristic flag `runtime.batch_grouping = adaptive_v2` flips the regression on/off. `adaptive_v1` (old) has expected numbers.
Sam: can we bisect the PR? 3382 is big (kernel selection + batching + a tiny kv change). Prioritize the batching heuristic.
Mae: I started a quick bisect on master -> 3382 locally. Early signs point to a change in `batching/group_by_seqlen()` that altered bucket thresholds.
Tanya: If it's bucket thresholds, the fix may be straightforward: restore the cutoff boundary for small-seq kernels (<16) and add an explicit cache-warm path when group toggles kernel mid-episode.
Oliver: Also the CI perf test `perftest/kvcache_end2end` is flaky — it reports different p99s depending on run order. I think the test harness doesn't sufficiently prepare the store (missing warmup).
Sam: Proposed immediate mitigations: 1) revert the batching change in 3382 for hotfix; 2) add an extra warmup phase (5k requests) to `perftest/kvcache_end2end` and bump p99 threshold to a safer margin while we stabilize; 3) add a targeted microbenchmark for short-seq batching to CI.
Mae: Agreed. I've opened a hotfix PR 3391 that reverts `adaptive_v2` and re-applies unrelated safe patches from 3382. Running CI now.
perf-bot: CI run triggered: https://ci.internal/runs/68512 — waiting for perf jobs (perftest/kvcache_end2end, perftest/batch_shortseq).
Rajiv: For the longer term: let's add a bench `bench/batch_shortseq_latency` that simulates skewed seq_len distribution (80% [1..8], 20% [32..128]) and measures kernel selection frequency + p99 over 1000 iterations. Make it part of PR gating.
Tanya: Also a couple of fixes for flaky tests: deterministic RNG seed for request generator, and disable parallel runs that share the same backend instance (they were contaminating cache hit rate).
Sam: I ran the profiler on the failing canary instance (perf sample):
Sam: ```
# top samples
choose_kernel_for_seq 48.5%
kv_cache::lookup_maybe 22.1%
gpu_dispatch 11.6%
batch_builder::assemble 8.4%
```
Sam: choose_kernel_for_seq is spending lots of time comparing bucketing heuristics, not cheap. We should memoize recent sequence-length -> kernel decisions for the duration of an execution stream.
Oliver: Good call. Memoization TTL should be per-connection or per-stream to avoid cross-request pollution. Add that as a follow-up.
Mae: Hotfix CI passed perf smoke (local canary bumped back to normal). I'm rolling the revert to canary now. deploy-bot: Rollout paused due to perf regression — manual override requested.
deploy-bot: Rollout action: manual-rollback applied by Mae at 1808004370. Canary restored to previous stable image.
Rajiv: I'll draft the microbench and put it behind a quick opt-in flag so it doesn't slow down everyone yet. Also adding an assertion in `choose_kernel_for_seq` logs when it switches kernel for >20% of batch. That will help us debug in future canaries.
Tanya: Action items:
- Mae: coordinate hotfix rollback and canary validation (done)
- Rajiv: PR for memoization + assertion + microbench (ETA: end of day tomorrow)
- Sam: update perftest harness: add 5k warmup + deterministic seed + disable parallelized same-backend runs (PR 3393)
- Oliver: create CI job `perftest/batch_shortseq` and tune thresholds (add baseline numbers)
- perf-bot: re-run nightly perf sweeps against master and hotfix branch and annotate flakiness if variance > 10%
Mae: Thanks all. If anyone sees residual elevated evictions after the rollback, ping me. :pray:
perf-bot: Nightly job scheduled: 1808080000
Oliver: we should also document the batching thresholds in docs/runtime/batching.md so future tweaks are explicit. I'll add a short section.
Mae: closing loop in here once the microbench is merged and CI stabilizes.
